cues.en: When I'm visiting a new city and I want to know if it has any chance of being great, the most important thing for me is walkability.
cues.zh: 当我来到一座新城市，想知道它有没有可能变得伟大时，对我来说最重要的一点就是步行友好度。

cues.en: Walkable neighborhoods are always the best. But the second most important thing is the answer to the question, do your buses
cues.zh: 适合步行的街区永远是最好的。但第二重要的，是要回答这个问题：你的公交车

cues.en: get stuck in traffic?
cues.zh: 会堵在路上吗？

cues.en: This one question reveals so much about a city's priorities and the way its citizens live.
cues.zh: 这一个问题就能揭示一座城市的优先级，以及市民的生活方式。

cues.en: Let me explain.
cues.zh: 让我解释一下。

cues.en: There's a term in urban planning called the Downs Thompson Paradox.
cues.zh: 城市规划里有个术语叫唐斯-汤普森悖论。

cues.en: The equilibrium speed of car traffic on a road network is determined by the average door to door speed of equivalent journeys taken by public transport.
cues.zh: 道路网络上汽车交通的均衡速度，取决于公共交通完成同等行程的平均门到门速度。

cues.en: Yeah. But it it basically means that it doesn't matter how many roads you build. Car traffic will get worse and worse and worse until it becomes faster to take the bus or the metro
cues.zh: 没错。但它基本上意味着，不管你建多少路，汽车交通都会越来越糟，直到坐公交、地铁

cues.en: or the tram.
cues.zh: 或有轨电车变得更快。

cues.en: You get the idea.
cues.zh: 你懂这个意思。

cues.en: And this isn't some academic curiosity either. It's been observed time and time again in cities all over the world.
cues.zh: 这也不是什么学术上的好奇。全世界的城市都一次又一次地观察到了这个现象。

cues.en: But while it might seem paradoxical
cues.zh: 虽然乍看之下似乎很矛盾，

cues.en: at first, it actually makes a lot of sense if you give it some thought.
cues.zh: 但仔细想想，其实非常合理。

cues.en: When it comes down to it, there really aren't that many car people,
cues.zh: 说到底，真正的汽车爱好者

cues.en: bicycle people,
cues.zh: 自行车爱好者、

cues.en: train people, or unicycle people.
cues.zh: 火车爱好者，或者独轮车爱好者，其实并没有那么多。

cues.en: The vast majority of people in the world just want to get from point a to point b as quickly and conveniently as possible.
cues.zh: 世界上绝大多数人，只是想尽可能快速、方便地从A点到达B点。

cues.en: Well, maybe not the unicycle people.
cues.zh: 好吧，独轮车爱好者可能除外。

cues.en: For Amsterdam,
cues.zh: 在阿姆斯特丹，

cues.en: it's often a bicycle.
cues.zh: 它往往是自行车。

cues.en: For Tokyo,
cues.zh: 在东京，

cues.en: it's usually a train.
cues.zh: 通常是火车。

cues.en: But for far too many of the world's cities,
cues.zh: 但对世界上太多城市来说，

cues.en: it's a car.
cues.zh: 它是汽车。

cues.en: And the reason for this is very clear.
cues.zh: 原因非常清楚。

cues.en: Why would anybody take this bus if it's going to get stuck in the same traffic as a car?
cues.zh: 如果公交车会像汽车一样堵在路上，谁还会去坐呢？

cues.en: The answer for most cities in The US and Canada is simple. You ride the bus because you're too poor to drive. If you had any choice, you wouldn't.
cues.zh: 对美国和加拿大多数城市来说，答案很简单。你坐公交是因为你太穷，开不起车。如果有得选，你才不会坐。

cues.en: When your public transportation is only used by the poor and the desperate, it's hard to get much support for it.
cues.zh: 当公共交通只有穷人和走投无路的人在用时，很难获得多少支持。

cues.en: People taking the bus are looked down upon and anybody wealthy enough to have any political influence whatsoever doesn't care about improving service.
cues.zh: 坐公交的人被人看不起，而任何有钱到有政治影响力的人，根本不在乎改善服务。

cues.en: If anything, they'll see public transportation as a nuisance, for instance complaining that the streetcars are in the way of their car.
cues.zh: 他们甚至会觉得公共交通是个麻烦，比如抱怨有轨电车挡了他们的车道。

cues.en: They just want it to go away.
cues.zh: 他们只想让它消失。

cues.en: This is the look, I don't care where the poor people go just as long as they're not in the way of my car approach to public transport.
cues.zh: 这就是那种“我不在乎穷人去哪，只要别挡我车道”的公共交通态度。

cues.en: Ultimately,
cues.zh: 最终，

cues.en: that means the city devolves into a mess of car traffic with giant gaps between the rich and the poor.
cues.zh: 这意味着城市沦为一片交通混乱，贫富差距巨大。

cues.en: But back to the paradox.
cues.zh: 但回到那个悖论。

cues.en: If buses and trams get stuck in traffic so it can never be faster to take the bus, then what happens to car traffic?
cues.zh: 如果公交和有轨电车会堵在路上，坐公交永远快不起来，那汽车交通会怎样？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: it increases
cues.zh: 它只会增加，

cues.en: almost indefinitely.
cues.zh: 几乎无限增加。

cues.en: And North American cities have continued to take on more and more debt to build roads they can't afford in an attempt to manage it.
cues.zh: 而北美城市为了应对，继续背负越来越多的债务，去修根本负担不起的道路。

cues.en: This is typical hourly traffic volumes in cities in The Netherlands with clear morning and evening rush hour.
cues.zh: 这是荷兰城市典型的每小时交通流量，早晚高峰清晰可见。

cues.en: However, in cities where there are no alternatives to driving, car traffic becomes so bad that people start leaving earlier and earlier.
cues.zh: 然而，在一些没有其他出行选择的城市，汽车交通变得非常糟糕，人们开始越来越早地出门。

cues.en: Pretty soon, rush hour
cues.zh: 很快，高峰时段

cues.en: morphs to become several hours long.
cues.zh: 就延长到了好几个小时。

cues.en: Here
cues.zh: 这里

cues.en: are 16 lanes of car traffic in Toronto, Canada.
cues.zh: 是加拿大温哥华的16条车道交通。

cues.en: This video was taken at two p. M. On a Tuesday
cues.zh: 这段视频拍摄于周二下午两点

cues.en: in the middle of summer holidays.
cues.zh: 正值暑假期间。

cues.en: Daytime traffic never gets better than this.
cues.zh: 白天的交通状况永远不会比这更好。

cues.en: Every one of these people had a choice of how they were going to get around that day but this city made decisions that meant that every single one of them had to choose a car.
cues.zh: 这些人中的每一个人当天都有选择如何出行的自由，但这座城市做出的决策意味着他们每一个人都不得不选择开车。

cues.en: So what's the solution?
cues.zh: 那么解决方案是什么？

cues.en: Thankfully,
cues.zh: 幸运的是，

cues.en: more and more cities are waking up to the problem and have started to do something about it. New York recently removed cars almost completely from 14th Street to speed up the buses.
cues.zh: 越来越多的城市开始意识到这个问题，并着手采取行动。纽约最近几乎完全禁止了14街的汽车通行，以加快公交速度。

cues.en: San Francisco recently did the same on Market Street.
cues.zh: 旧金山最近在市场街也采取了同样的措施。

cues.en: And Toronto removed most of the cars from King Street which has significantly increased streetcar ridership.
cues.zh: 多伦多则移除了King Street的大部分汽车，这大幅增加了有轨电车的乘客量。

cues.en: What's also interesting is that while the Downs Thompson Paradox was originally described for public transportation,
cues.zh: 同样有趣的是，虽然唐斯-汤普森悖论最初是针对公共交通描述的，

cues.en: it actually applies to any alternative.
cues.zh: 但它实际上适用于任何替代方案。

cues.en: If it's more convenient to take a bicycle, then some people will switch to a bicycle,
cues.zh: 如果骑自行车更方便，那么一些人就会转而骑自行车，

cues.en: as is common in parts of The Netherlands and Denmark.
cues.zh: 这在荷兰和丹麦的部分地区很常见。

cues.en: And if it's faster to walk, then people will walk.
cues.zh: 如果走路更快，人们就会走路。

cues.en: An incredible statistic is that 40% of people who live in Downtown Toronto walk to work because most people feel unsafe cycling and traffic has become so bad that it's literally faster to walk.
cues.zh: 一个惊人的数据是，住在多伦多市中心的人有40%步行上班，因为大多数人觉得骑车不安全，而交通已经糟糕到走路确实更快。

cues.en: So any alternative to driving has the ability to reduce car traffic.
cues.zh: 所以任何替代开车的方案都能减少汽车交通。

cues.en: It doesn't mean that everybody has to take the bus or that everybody has to ride a bicycle.
cues.zh: 这并不意味着每个人都必须坐公交，或者每个人都必须骑自行车。

cues.en: Even the Autolua areas in The Netherlands allow some motor vehicles.
cues.zh: 就连荷兰的Autolua区域也允许一些机动车通行。

cues.en: But making the alternatives faster for even a segment of the population
cues.zh: 但只要让替代方案对哪怕一部分人来说更快

cues.en: can lead to significant improvements
cues.zh: 就能带来显著的改善

cues.en: and some Dutch cities like Amsterdam do this really well.
cues.zh: 而阿姆斯特丹等一些荷兰城市在这方面做得非常好。

cues.en: I occasionally hear drivers in The Netherlands complaining that they have to take circuitous routes through the city to get to their destination
cues.zh: 我偶尔听到荷兰的司机抱怨，他们不得不绕路穿过城市才能到达目的地

cues.en: or that they have to wait while bicycles and trams get priority.
cues.zh: 或者他们不得不等待，而自行车和有轨电车享有优先权。

cues.en: But I assure you the alternative is worse.
cues.zh: 但我向你保证，另一种情况更糟。

cues.en: If taking a car becomes quick and convenient, then all these people on trams and bicycles will take a car too. And that direct route will become slower to drive than today's indirect route.
cues.zh: 如果开车变得快捷方便，那么所有这些坐有轨电车和骑自行车的人也会去开车。而那条直达路线开车会比今天的绕行路线更慢。

cues.en: Not to mention all the other problems that come along with an increase in car traffic in the city.
cues.zh: 更不用说城市汽车交通增加所带来的所有其他问题了。

cues.en: So the next time you're sitting in traffic and see the bus speed by in the priority lane, remember the Downs Thompson paradox
cues.zh: 所以下次你堵在路上，看到公交车在优先车道飞驰而过时，记住唐斯-汤普森悖论

cues.en: and be glad you're not driving
cues.zh: 并庆幸你没有开车

cues.en: in this.
cues.zh: 在这样的路上。
